book_summary: 1 Chronicles is complete across chapters 1-29 in restored/source-audited draft and mystical companion layers. The book moves from Adam, nations, Israelite and neighboring genealogies through postexilic Jerusalem, Saul's death, David's coronation and warrior traditions, ark processions, worship organization, Davidic covenant, imperial wars, Ammonite humiliation and Rabbah, census plague, Ornan's threshing floor, temple preparation, Levitical and priestly divisions, musicians, gatekeepers, treasuries, military and agricultural administration, public succession, donations, Solomon's anointing, and David's death. Safeguards reject racialized genealogy, blood purity, inherited guilt, Amalek targeting, patriarchy, slavery and coerced marriage, fertility hierarchy, disability stigma, militarism, leader cult, suicide misuse, medium persecution, conquest entitlement, sacred violence, worker blaming, anointed-leader immunity, religious persecution, imperial expansion, animal harm invisibility, plague punishment, coerced migrant labor, clerical caste, exploitative worship labor, war-wealth laundering, authoritarian spiritual blueprints, coerced giving, prosperity fundraising, and the absolution of David through idealized memory.

translation_notes: Genealogies are selective archives, not racial hierarchies, citizenship tests, blood-purity systems, or complete biological records.

Women, unnamed daughters, concubines, enslaved or servile people, migrants, artisans, scribes, farmers, musicians, gatekeepers, cooks, treasurers, and animal keepers must not disappear behind elite male names.
Ancient names such as Amalek, Philistine, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Hagarite, Ishmaelite, Jebusite, Aramean, and Canaanite may never be mapped onto living peoples as inherited enemies.
Military censuses, body counts, warrior lists, conquest, garrisons, tribute, plunder, and fear do not establish moral greatness.
David's chosen or anointed status never removes accountability for Bathsheba, Uriah, Tamar, conquest, forced labor, census deaths, or institutional pressure.
Saul's and the armor-bearer's deaths are suicide-sensitive tragedy, never models or proof of mental-illness stigma.
Uzzah's death and Nadab/Abihu traditions are sacred violence and may not support fear-based religion or worker blaming.
'Touch not my anointed' protects vulnerable figures in liturgical memory and may never shield abusive leaders.
The Davidic covenant remains Jewish covenantal scripture and may not be superseded, converted into divine-right monarchy, or used for modern territorial claims.
Land promises and settlement lists are ancient identity memory, not deeds authorizing displacement of present residents.

Temple grandeur rests on materials, ecosystems, migrant labor, skilled work, food systems, animals, and administration; spiritual purpose increases obligations for consent, safety, accessibility, fair pay, and transparency.
War spoil and royal donations do not launder violence or purchase absolution.
Census plague language may not support epidemic-punishment theology; the ethical center is the command to stop destruction.
Lots, spiritual blueprints, inspired music, and heart-searching language do not replace evidence, engineering, consent, financial controls, or freedom of conscience.
Voluntary giving must remain genuinely voluntary, especially under royal, public, family, or religious pressure.
David's good death, riches, honor, and idealized archives do not erase survivors and communities harmed during his reign.
Mystical companion layers remain interpretive and never replace restored/source-audited text.
